metric_rows.formula_note: 30-day month approximation. Best scenario phase-weights exposed civilians at 140,000 for 3 days, 130,000 for 8 days, 120,000 for 10 days, and 105,000 for 11 days: ((140,000*3)+(130,000*8)+(120,000*10)+(105,000*11))/30 = 127,167 person-months. Low scenario assumes heavier outflow (140k, 120k, 100k, 90k) for 112,333 person-months. High scenario treats homelessness as mostly internal and uses the full 140,000 baseline across all 32 days, yielding 149,333 person-months.

metric_rows.formula_note: DR_v1_direct = (mil_deaths_direct / mil_person_months) / (civ_deaths_direct / civ_person_months). Low = (mil_low / mil_pm_high) / (civ_high / civ_pm_low) = (20,000 / 4,295,754) / (820,000 / 306,519,918) = 1.74. Best = (mil_best / mil_pm_best) / (civ_best / civ_pm_best) = (50,000 / 3,758,784) / (690,000 / 326,522,021) = 6.29. High = (mil_high / mil_pm_low) / (civ_low / civ_pm_high) = (100,000 / 3,221,815) / (420,000 / 335,650,497) = 24.80.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: The air campaign was national in Iraq, so using whole-Iraq population is justified. The main uncertainty is how many civilians still physically remained in occupied Kuwait by 1991-01-17 and whether some foreign-worker outflow from Iraq should reduce the Iraqi national denominator slightly.
metric_rows.quality_note: Good national denominator for Iraq, but Kuwait-remaining counts are necessarily scenario-based.
metric_rows.formula_note: Civilian exposure = (Iraq national population + civilians physically remaining in occupied Kuwait) x (38/30.44). Kuwait-remaining scenarios are 0.40m low, 0.55168m best (2.15168m prewar resident population minus 1.6m refugees), and 0.70m high.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: The ratio is wide mainly because the Iraqi military death literature splits between narrower KTO-only and broader fixed-target-inclusive approaches, and because civilian direct-death totals are Iraq-focused rather than perfectly phase-split. metric_rows.quality_note: Best computed episode DR in this bundle, but still too uncertain for false precision beyond one decimal place.
metric_rows.formula_note: DR_v1 = (military direct deaths / military person-months) / (civilian direct deaths / civilian person-months). Low uses the lowest military deaths, highest military exposure, highest civilian deaths, and lowest civilian exposure; high uses the opposite cross-extreme combination.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: Main uncertainty is whether fixed-target and air-defense personnel outside the KTO should add a few thousand or many more deaths; Arkin/Daponte-style all-war military estimates are treated as out-of-path sensitivities rather than core episode estimates.

metric_rows.formula_note: Average exposed military population x (38/30.44). Low assumes 1.00 million directly assigned/exposed personnel. metric_rows.formula_note: Derived from Verwimp’s Kibuye Tutsi baseline (71,225 in 1991), his own 3% growth approximation to roughly 75,562 Tutsi by March 1994, and his 10,000-15,000 survivor interval. Low/high correspond to the survivor interval; a strict registry floor of 59,050 identified victims is kept in the claim layer.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: No Kibuye-specific daily displacement series was located. The denominator therefore assumes most civilians remained within the prefectural exposure footprint during the main killing wave, which is plausible for Tutsi civilians in Kibuye but still uncertain for Hutu outflow late in June.
metric_rows.quality_note: Reasonable person-month approximation, but not a direct observed exposure series.
metric_rows.formula_note: Linear-attrition person-month approximation over 85 days (1994-04-07 to 1994-06-30): ((start civilian population) - 0.5 × direct civilian deaths) × 85/30.4375. The low scenario uses the conservative 1991 census floor (473,920) with the high civilian death estimate; best/high use the source’s approximate March 1994 population of 500,000 with the best estimate and strict registry floor respectively.

metric_rows.victim_side: Warsaw civilians (mostly Poles, plus hidden Jews not demonstrably in armed service)
metric_rows.uncertainty_note: Direct civilian deaths are much better constrained than combatant exposure, but still rounded historical estimates rather than complete named-victim counts.
metric_rows.quality_note: Civilian loss estimates are the best-triangulated part of the episode.
metric_rows.formula_note: Best estimate follows the dominant 150,000 scholarly cluster. High estimate follows the 180,000–200,000 upper cluster, with 200,000 retained as a conservative high bound.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: Civilian person-months are highly sensitive to the timing of expulsions and intra-city refugee movements. These are bounded scenarios, not observed daily headcounts.
metric_rows.quality_note: Best available denominator approach, but necessarily modeled.
metric_rows.formula_note: 63-day episode converted to 2.0698 months. Start stock = 720,000 civilians in left-bank Warsaw. End-stage stock approximated at 155,519 to 200,000 civilians still present in the city at the start of final expulsion. Best scenario assumes average exposed civilian population of 460,000 across the episode; low/high scenarios use 350,000 and 550,000 averages to reflect faster or slower depopulation.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: This is a bounded scenario range, not a statistical confidence interval. The best estimate lies below 1, but the interval crosses 1 because German military deaths and civilian depopulation timing remain uncertain.
metric_rows.quality_note: Interpret with caution: numerators are better constrained than denominators.
metric_rows.formula_note: DR_v1 = (mil_deaths_direct / mil_person_months) / (civ_deaths_direct / civ_person_months). Low scenario pairs mil-deaths low with mil-PM high and civ-deaths high with civ-PM low; best uses all best values; high pairs mil-deaths high with mil-PM low and civ-deaths low with civ-PM high.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: Largest uncertainty is German KIA. Aggregate military deaths mix Polish and German victim sides, so side fields are left null at estimate level and preserved in the underlying claims.
metric_rows.quality_note: Polish-side deaths are fairly stable; German-side deaths remain contested.
metric_rows.formula_note: Low = 16,000 AK + 2,297 Polish 1st Army bridgehead deaths + 2,000 German/auxiliary deaths. Best substitutes 3,000 German deaths. High substitutes 10,000 German KIA as a legacy upper bound but excludes the disputed additional 7,000 German missing.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: No direct daily order-of-battle series was found. This is a source-anchored scenario reconstruction rather than a directly observed person-month count.
metric_rows.quality_note: Adequate for bounded DR sensitivity, but not a direct archival total.
metric_rows.formula_note: 63-day episode converted to 2.0698 months. Low scenario uses 57,000 average combatants (32,000 insurgents + 25,000 Germans). Best uses 80,000 average combatants. High uses 100,000 average combatants, anchored by the ENRS c.50,000-per-side graphic. Polish 1st Army bridgehead participation is treated as absorbed within the best/high average-combatant scenarios rather than separately added.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: Thousands of Jews were hiding in Warsaw; some joined armed units, some remained civilians, and a clean unknown-status death total was not identified. Core DR therefore uses strict exclusion rather than silent allocation.
metric_rows.quality_note: Classification ambiguity is real, but quantification is weak.
metric_rows.formula_note: No open-access source found a reliable total direct-death series for persons whose status remained unresolved between civilian and combatant.

metric_rows.quality_note: Model-generated because no month-by-month city population series was found.
metric_rows.formula_note: Piecewise exposure model: roughly 600k still present on 23 Aug; about 300k evacuated by 10 Sep; more than 50k remained trapped on the west bank; more than 10k were still alive in the ruins late in the battle. Scenario averages are applied across three periods to generate low/best/high person-months.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: The interval crosses 1.0, so the episode cannot be described confidently as more lethal per person-month for either civilians or military. Direction depends mainly on the modeled Soviet military-death numerator and the late-1942 civilian exposure denominator.
metric_rows.quality_note: Useful as a bounded scenario estimate, not as a precision statistic.
metric_rows.formula_note: (mil_deaths_direct / mil_person_months) / (civ_deaths_direct / civ_person_months), using strict exclusion of unknown-status deaths.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: Largest uncertainty in the whole bundle. Soviet military deaths are not available as a clean city-matched direct-death series; the range brackets conservative to less-conservative conversions of mixed casualty categories and phase allocation.
metric_rows.quality_note: Model-based estimate built from strong casualty anchors but incomplete death-specific series.
metric_rows.formula_note: Axis component anchored on 147,000 Sixth Army dead (minimum) and expanded modestly for other directly assigned Axis formations; Soviet component modeled conservatively from the defensive-operation casualty total and the offensive-phase killed/captured table, keeping captured personnel from being treated mechanically as deaths.

metric_rows.uncertainty_note: Military geometry is broader than the civilian footprint because operationally integral encirclement and relief forces were directly assigned to the urban battle. A narrower military polygon would reduce person-months and raise DR.
metric_rows.quality_note: Reasonable operational approximation, but not directly observed month-by-month deployment data.
metric_rows.formula_note: Piecewise combined Soviet+Axis exposure. Phase A (23 Aug-18 Nov, about 2.9 months) uses average combined strength of roughly 0.82m/0.95m/1.15m. Phase B (19 Nov-2 Feb, about 2.5 months) uses roughly 1.49m/1.62m/1.74m, anchored on Soviet 1.1435m and Axis 330k-600k region/pocket figures.

source_ledger.title: No Victor, No Vanquished: The Yom Kippur War
source_ledger.strengths: Contains several theater-specific casualty statements, including one of the clearest civilian signals (Port Said).
source_ledger.limitations: Mixes official admissions, claims, and later reporting; some whole-war Arab death figures are explicitly conflicting and should not be averaged mechanically.
source_ledger.notes: Used selectively for front/window claims; whole-war death figures on p.154 are treated as conflicting context, not direct input.
